title: After Bhuvneshwar's Recall at 36, Raina Backs Mohammed Shami for India Comeback
excerpt: The former India batter says Shami is "right behind" Bhuvneshwar Kumar after Bhuvi's age-36 recall — but his comeback case rests on domestic form, not Raina's endorsement.
body:
• Suresh Raina has backed Mohammed Shami for an India comeback, saying the pacer is "right behind" Bhuvneshwar Kumar after Bhuvi's recall to the T20I squad for the New Zealand series at age 36.
  • Shami last played for India in the Champions Trophy 2025 and last featured in Tests in the 2023 World Test Championship final; he has stayed active in domestic cricket and will open Bengal's 2026-27 Ranji Trophy campaign.
  • The door is ajar: selectors are yet to name the ODI and Test squads for the New Zealand tour, and injuries to Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana and Hardik Pandya have thinned the pace options.
  • Temper the excitement: Raina's backing is a personal assessment, not a BCCI decision — and Shami's recent IPL returns (18 wickets in 22 matches at an economy of 10) are a real concern.

Former India batter Suresh Raina believes Mohammed Shami could be on the verge of an international comeback — and he said it in Hindi, with the confidence of a man who has seen it happen before. Speaking at the jersey launch of the Indian Soft Ball Cricket League, Raina pointed to Bhuvneshwar Kumar's recall to India's T20I squad for the New Zealand tour at the age of 36 as the template.

"Making it to the Indian team at the age of 36 shows character. He has been a very disciplined bowler and a very process-driven guy who has worked really hard on his body," Raina said of Bhuvneshwar. Then came the line that set social media alight: "Absolutely, I think he (Mohammed Shami) has done well and played good domestic cricket too. Now it is Bhuvi's turn, aur Shami bhi aa rahe hain pichhe pichhe, tension mat lijiye" — Shami is right behind him, don't worry. Raina added that he hopes the selectors give Shami an opportunity.

"Absolutely, I think he has done well and played good domestic cricket too. Now it is Bhuvi's turn, aur Shami bhi aa rahe hain pichhe pichhe, tension mat lijiye."

— Suresh Raina (via PTI)

The case for Shami

The numbers that matter are the ones from domestic cricket. Shami has remained active since his last India appearance at the Champions Trophy 2025, playing domestic competitions and keeping himself in the conversation. He is set to represent Bengal in the opening fixture of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season — exactly the kind of red-ball statement a comeback campaign needs.

https://x.com/sportstarweb/status/2109188514894242013

The timing helps. The selectors have not yet announced the squads for the ODI and Test series against New Zealand, and the pace cupboard is thinner than usual: Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana and Hardik Pandya are all recovering from injuries. Bhuvneshwar's recall at 36 has established the precedent that the current selection thinking rewards discipline and domestic form over age. With Ajit Agarkar's exit from the selection setup, the dynamics of who gets picked have shifted further.

The case for caution

Three facts argue against getting carried away. First, Shami's recent IPL returns have been poor: 18 wickets in 22 matches across the 2025 and 2026 seasons at an economy rate of 10 runs per over. Second, his last Test appearance was the World Test Championship final against Australia in June 2023 — more than three years ago. Third, and most important: Raina's remarks are a personal assessment, not information from the selection room. The BCCI has said nothing about Shami's future, and former players backing comebacks is a genre with a long history of being wrong.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=5CkUwkKCRwY

Diaspora angle

For the diaspora's cricket fans — from the Bay Area to Brampton — the New Zealand tour is one of the season's marquee fixtures, and a Shami-Bhuvneshwar veteran pace attack would be pure theatre. If Shami makes the Test squad, his first outing would be a genuine event: the return of one of India's great modern fast bowlers after years in the wilderness.

What's next

The ODI and Test squads for the New Zealand tour are expected shortly. Shami's Ranji Trophy opener for Bengal is his audition in whites. If he takes wickets and stays fit, Raina's "piche piche" prediction gets a real hearing; if not, it joins the long list of comeback talk that never made it past the press conference.
